notes.title: Scaredy Cat Development Pause: Release Date on Hold
notes.content:
Development Update

Hey everyone,

It’s not the update I hoped to share, but due to personal circumstances, all development on Scaredy Cat is currently on hold. The previously mentioned release window of June 2025 is no longer accurate, and a new date hasn’t been set.

This decision wasn't made lightly, but it’s necessary. Creating this game with care, quality and authenticity takes stability and time - and right now, that means stepping away for a bit. Scaredy Cat is deeply personal, and I hope to return to it when it can get the focus it deserves.

To everyone who playtested the demo, left feedback or helped shape the game in any way: thank you. Your thoughts, encouragement and belief in Scaredy Cat have truly kept it going through the hardest moments. It means so much that this weird, heartfelt, dark little game has found its people.

Updates will be posted when development resumes. Henny will have to stay lonely for just a little bit longer.

Our socials will be kept live, but quieter during this period:

Sincerely,

notes.title: Scaredy Cat Release Update: New Launch Target Set for Valentine's Day 2025
notes.content:
Release Update
I’d like to let everyone know that the release date for Scaredy Cat has been slightly extended to early 2025. We’re now aiming for a Valentine’s Day launch and will keep you updated on our progress. (This will align nicely with the in-game timeline, too! 💝)

While I know many of you were excited for a December release, our goal is to deliver the experience we imagined. The extra time will also allow us to integrate feedback from the demo and Next Fest, ensuring the game meets our highest standards. 

To everyone who has wishlisted Scaredy Cat, followed our development, or tried the demo: your support has been invaluable and truly motivating. We can’t wait for you to experience the full journey of Henny and Conhaven.

notes.title: Mid-Summer Dev Updates for Scaredy Cat
notes.content:
Hi everyone,

I'm excited to share the latest in Scaredy Cat's development! Since our May devlog, the focus has been on polishing and enhancing the demo content, which you'll have the opportunity to play shortly and definitely by the Steam Next Fest this October (14-21).

Here's a breakdown of recent progress:

✨ Demo-Specific Enhancements
- A thorough consistency pass on the quests featured in the demo, ensuring they all have proper progression, alerts, sounds and polish elements. (Internally, we've created a quest template and standardized process for new quest introductions - this makes it easier to spin up quests in-engine!)
- Additional side quests have been introduced and refined for the demo, adding more depth to the world
- More conditional dialogues for clue, puzzle and world objects, enhancing interactivity and narrative integration in the demo areas (Translation: For all you narrative nerds, you'll get different information from items depending at what stage you are in your playthrough.)
- In general, the game has undergone a visual lift to prepare for the demo, including new art assets, light and shadow review, SFX, particles and interaction feedback
- New audio elements have been added, including animal and interactable object sounds to bring the demo areas to life and provide more audio feedback
- More cinematic flair introduced to support moments with strong narrative beats such as replaying a flashback
- General updating of placeholder content such as characters, UI, draft dialogues

{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44964289/6c067356e4eef29d0d7749e2296d46680c45ec31.jpg

🧩 Puzzle and Gameplay Improvements for the Demo
- New puzzles have been added to one of the demo areas, increasing the variety of challenges players will face
- The office puzzle has been tweaked and refined for a better player experience, with the aim of tutorializing some of the later gameplay you'll experience whilst pet-sitting for different owners

🐶 NPC and Pet Behavior in Demo Areas
- After iterating on levels/puzzles, several updates have been made to pet stats, behavior and puzzles to make the demo levels feel cohesive
- An important new NPC has been added to the game in a chain of side quests, expanding the cast of characters you'll meet and teasing future relationships

{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44964289/2c93bafd3b11b33f169b0199200612e7c8a50caa.jpg

📖 UI and Quality of Life Improvements
- The Quest Journal and HUD have received updates for better usability, which you'll experience in the demo
- We've made improvements to the Dialogue and Text Message UIs to improve accessibility and give more narrative flavor

🐛 Bug Fixes and Optimizations
- Fixed various bugs, including issues with wanderer scripts, teleporters, and dialogue triggers to ensure a polished demo
- Refactoring of some major gameplay systems to optimize and make more usable in future projects

We're excited to have you experience this slice of Scaredy Cat during Steam Next Fest this October. This demo represents significant chunk of the vision for the game, which is intended to be a more engaging and narratively rich experience.

Your support through engagement and wishlists has been invaluable in getting us to this point! ❤️
If you haven't already, wishlist Scaredy Cat for when the demo drops, and mark your calendars for Steam Next Fest in October!

notes.title: Late May Dev Updates for Scaredy Cat
notes.content:
Hi all,

Rapid progress has been made on Scaredy Cat over the past few weeks with strides in NPC AI, refining existing systems, LOTS of (heavy and darkly funny) writing and designing engaging, well-integrated narrative and level/puzzle content.

Here's a breakdown of our recent developments:

👯‍♀️ Integration of Story and Level/Puzzle Design 

As a narrative designer, tying the story into the (best suited style of) gameplay in a satisfying and natural way has been one of the most fun (sometimes, type 2 fun) challenges on Scaredy Cat. Therefore, much of this dev cycle has been iterating on this.

- Introduced a series of cognitive and environmental puzzles that complement the narrative into each level - leaning into more puzzle-oriented levels fits the mystery genre and breaks up the pace of gameplay
- Wrote and implemented narrative content to support each level, including NPC conversations, clue object text, puzzle dialogue and barks
- Brought several important game locations to life including Conhaven downtown with distinct districts, a city park, Aerocorp headquarters, new hospital variant for a childhood memory scene
- Refined the flow for the first level (Camille's Loft) which helped better inform the narrative delivery strategy across the remaining levels
- Set up quest scaffolding to support levels and updated quest assets for each pet-sitting level location

✨ Spectacle! 

- Added new art assets, which included more urban assets such as moving trains and city props, to signficantly overhaul Conhaven, the main city hub A little video clip.
- Implemented a subtle dust trail effect behind the player, which updates based on their velocity if they are in an outdoor environment 
- Improvements to sky object spawning system (changed from cloud spawning to a generic sky spawning system) so it can support all types of objects moving overhead - more randomness and variability in results Click for GIF.
- Experimented with new monster sprites
- Wind shader has been applied to some nature and other environmental dressing to create a more immersive atmosphere Click for GIFs.
- Iterations to lighting and post-processing to enhance the game's visual appeal, as well as an improved lighting workflow for quicker scene dressing 

🤖 NPC AI 

- Implemented follower and wanderer scripts for navmesh AI and set up animator override controllers for wanderers/followers Wanderer GIF.
- Added functionality to send NPCs away or to another target if they are engaged in conversation while wandering
- Set up navmeshes for several areas to test with pets and other NPCs

🔊 Audio and Immersion 

- Introduced spatial audio for more dynamic experience
- Implemented audio for walking on different surfaces and added sound effects to various objects, such as the arcade machine

Misc: UI Quality of Life Improvements, Bug Fixes

- Updated the UI for the dialogue system and made changes to the journal UI for a better user experience
- Fixed various bugs, such as issues with wanderer scripts and teleporters, and teleport issue caused by no default cam zoom being set

Upcoming Developments

The coming weeks on Scaredy Cat are about refining gameplay mechanics, implementing more narrative content and polishing the overall experience. I'll likely be taking more of a break from social channels to really focus on making Scaredy Cat the best it can be, but will try to squeeze in smaller development updates on the below channels:

X: @aeiogames
Threads: @aeiogames
TikTok: @aeiogames
YouTube: aeio_games
Instagram: @aeiogames
Bluesky: @aeiogames.bsky.social

Thank you for your continued support and interest in Scaredy Cat. If there's something specific you'd like to hear more about - about the characters and lore of the world, other gameplay specifics, whatever's on your mind - drop a comment and we'll do our best to bring you the updates you're most curious about.

Sincerely,
Mel and the Scaredy Cat Team 🖤

notes.title: Early Spring Dev Updates for Scaredy Cat
notes.content:
Early Spring Dev Updates for Scaredy Cat

Hi all,

With so many developments on Scaredy Cat over the past few months, we wanted to share it all with the Steam community. Aside from getting the Scaredy Cat Steam page up and running, we've been hard at work implementing new features, refining existing systems and creating narrative and level content to bring the game to life.

Quest System and Narrative Progress

One of our primary focuses has been on enhancing the game's narrative and questing systems. We've implemented the Quest Machine plugin from Pixel Crushers (along with Dialogue System for Unity) to streamline quest creation and management. We've also smoothened our workflow for creating new NPCs and objects that trigger quest and dialogue events, laying a solid foundation for the game's questing system.

The dialogue database has been expanded with narrative content including conditions, enabling more dynamic conversations based on the game state. This, combined with the implementation of character art, conversations and clues in each level, has significantly enhanced the game experience.

Furthermore, all narrative planning and level design has now been planned for Scaredy Cat. (Including the cumbersome task on settling on names for all owners, pets and monsters!) Much of this has already started to be implemented in-game.

{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44964289/9a50a1f8f5f1c4ec30f074a4a7d5c711be7aee77.png

Improved Visuals and Atmosphere

To create a more immersive, engaging experience that matches the intended tone for Scaredy Cat, we've made several improvements to the visuals and atmosphere. New art assets for animals have been added and strategically placed them throughout the game world. Some examples include a cat in the downtown scene and floating swans in various locations. A cloud shadow spawning system has been introduced which combined with time of day and weather, adds a nice touch to the world.

We've also laid out several new locations (grocery store, two homes which will serve as levels) and enhanced others, such as the office environment. With improved lighting, decor and NPC barks, these locations now feel more realistic and interesting.

{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44964289/cd9797249b7d13147642ef047cb2a93e61912e38.jpg

{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44964289/eeb5037456534e01064920a1dafddca232b04f68.png

{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44964289/8799aa3e43dd2fb5a9f4602b64c4c8214c265ea7.jpg

UI Updates and Quest Journal

We've made updates to the quest heading text and layout, making it clearer and more visually appealing for players. Additionally, we've done iterations on the design the Quest Journal UI, which will serve as a helpful reference for tracking their progress and objectives throughout the game.

Teleportation System

To facilitate smooth navigation between major areas within the starting zone, we've finished implementing the teleportation functionality. We've set up teleporters that connect these areas and added fades between teleports to make the transitions less jarring. The function that handles player teleportation, zone change and camera update logic can be called from other scripts in the future, which will be particularly handy for story moments.

Gameplay Enhancements and Bug Fixes

In addition to the visual improvements, we've made several gameplay enhancements and bug fixes, including ensuring save data is capturing important variables for testing. 

We've implemented audio for walking on different surfaces, providing a more immersive experience. We also fixed a movement bug that allowed players to move while engaged in a conversation, ensuring a smoother gameplay experience.

To make transitions between areas more polished, we've implemented a small feature that pauses player movement when transitioning between areas. This helps to create a more seamless experience  as you navigate the game world.

Upcoming Developments

As we move forward, we're excited to continue refining and expanding the game to round the experience before early testing. Stay tuned for future devlog-type updates. The next big focus is going to be carrying on with narrative implementation and hooking things up across all levels.

For smaller, more frequent Scaredy Cat updates, be sure to check out our social media:

Twitter: @aeiogames
Threads: @aeiogames
Instagram: @aeiogames
TikTok: @howtomakeagame (This is a less formal channel - but still sharing SC updates regularly).

Thank you to everyone who has helped grow Scaredy Cat's Steam Wishlist. 🖤 Your support means the world to us, and we can't wait to share more of this unique, narrative-driven experience with you. If you're drawn to sad stories and conspiracies, Scaredy Cat is definitely the game for you!

Until next time,
Mel and the Scaredy Cat Team
